wants.topic: Deities directly interacting with and being tested by humble, poor, or elderly devotees
wants.evidence: GuruVaani Studio's video about Maa Durga doing housework for an old woman achieved a 256.95x vsNormal rating, and Chhathi Maiya helping a poor mother reached 58.18x vsNormal.

wants.topic: Deep theological questions explaining Hindu concepts (e.g., why Hinduism has multiple deities, omnipresence of Ishwar)
wants.evidence: Bk Usha Motivational video 'हिंदू धर्म में इतने भगवान...' achieved 132.33x vsNormal.

wants.topic: Multi-part impossible swayamvar challenges involving humble protagonists overcoming arrogant royal conditions
wants.evidence: THE BH STORIES 'घमंडी राजकुमारी का स्वयंवर' parts 1-3 dominated channel views with vsNormal up to 32.74x.

wants.topic: Seasonal Vrat Kathas emphasizing emotional family bonds (Bhai Dooj sibling stories, Chhath Puja, Karwa Chauth)
wants.evidence: FaKT Dharmik Katha's Karwa Chauth (11.04x vsNormal) and Bhai Dooj (8.97x vsNormal) outperformed all their standard daily upload content.

wants.topic: Lighthearted, playful divine leelas featuring gods in domestic, relatable scenarios (gods cooking, sticking to funny household rules)
wants.evidence: JagaLeela Studio's Adhaiya series videos ('आज खाना भगवान बनाएंगे!') consistently earned 8x-9x vsNormal compared to their standard Jagannath stories.

gaps: Relatable emotional dramas connecting major Hindu festivals (Navratri, Chhath) with real-life family hardships rather than just static ritual recitations.
Engaging, narrative-driven answers to common philosophical questions about Hindu scriptures and iconography.
Humorous yet respectful character-driven divine animation (banter between cute devotees and deities) with complete narrative arcs.
saturated: Generic motivational shorts/reels with generic audio clips.
Dry, chapter-by-chapter daily scripture readings (e.g., Kartik Maas Adhyay series) without emotional hooks.
Absurd or bizarre fairytale mashups disconnected from traditional mythological roots (e.g., princess marrying a turtle).
Standard routine Ekadashi audio recitals lacking custom visual storytelling.
